key_insight: ADSMoE identified four biologically and clinically distinct Alzheimer’s disease subtypes from incomplete multimodal data.
clinical_relevance: The subtypes could support future Alzheimer’s disease stratification and biomarker research, but clinical utility is not established.
method: Uses a mixture-of-experts transformer autoencoder to learn multimodal disease signatures.
Handles varying combinations of available modalities with a Fleximodal MoE encoder.
Captures complementary subtype characteristics with a subtype-specific MoE decoder.
evidence_signal: Across 5,422 participants in three cohorts, ADSMoE was trained on ADNI and externally validated in NACC and UKB without retraining, showing consistent subtype-associated characteristics.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether subtype assignments improve prospective clinical decisions or treatment outcomes.
paper_title: ADSMoE: A mixture-of-experts-based transformer autoencoder for discovering multimodal Alzheimer's disease subtypes
